cli.usage:
usage: mcp-n4 [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
              [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS] [--max-writes N]
              [--auth-cooldown SECONDS] [--load-wait SECONDS]
              [--http-timeout SECONDS] [--station NAME=URL]
              [--station-home NAME=PATH] [--niagara-home NAME=PATH]
              [--credential-env PREFIX] [--insecure-tls NAME]
              [--allow-tier-b NAME] [--allow-tier-c NAME]
              [--progress-file PATH] [--allow-http-for-tests]
cli.help:
usage: mcp-n4 [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
              [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS] [--max-writes N]
              [--auth-cooldown SECONDS] [--load-wait SECONDS]
              [--http-timeout SECONDS] [--station NAME=URL]
              [--station-home NAME=PATH] [--niagara-home NAME=PATH]
              [--credential-env PREFIX] [--insecure-tls NAME]
              [--allow-tier-b NAME] [--allow-tier-c NAME]
              [--progress-file PATH] [--allow-http-for-tests]

Stdio MCP server for Niagara N4 stations (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). Run
the `mcp-n4` binary: starting it prints nothing and contacts no station. MCP
protocol versions: this server speaks 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05
(`server.protocol_versions` of the registry). A client asking for a newer
revision is answered with 2025-06-18. Only add a newer revision to that list
once its semantics (new message shapes, capabilities, required fields) are
implemented and tested here.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --allow-writes        register the write tools (dry run + confirmation token
                        each)
  --write-scope ORD_PREFIX
                        ORD prefix writes may touch (repeatable); none = no
                        writes
  --state-dir STATE_DIR
                        journal/audit directory (default
                        ~/.local/state/mcp-n4)
  --token-ttl SECONDS   confirmation token lifetime (default 300)
  --max-writes N        executed writes allowed per server process (default
                        200); a reconnect does not reset it
  --auth-cooldown SECONDS
                        after an authentication failure, refuse station calls
                        this long (default and minimum 30: the lock-out
                        window)
  --load-wait SECONDS   total wait for one component load (default 3; 1-60):
                        raise it for a slow or remote station
  --http-timeout SECONDS
                        HTTP timeout of one station request (default 20;
                        5-300)
  --station NAME=URL    station n4_connect may use (repeatable); NAME should
                        equal the station's stationName; URL must be https://
  --station-home NAME=PATH
                        directory holding the config.bog of configured station
                        NAME; lets n4_save_station prove persistence
                        (repeatable)
  --niagara-home NAME=PATH
                        Niagara installation directory of configured station
                        NAME, reachable from this machine (the one holding
                        security/licenses); lets n4_license_info add when
                        each licence was generated and its version
                        (repeatable)
  --credential-env PREFIX
                        env var prefix holding <PREFIX>_USER/<PREFIX>_PASSWORD
                        (default MCP_N4)
  --insecure-tls NAME   skip TLS certificate verification for this configured
                        station (self-signed); repeatable
  --allow-tier-b NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier B (4.15/4.3); only after a PoC matched
                        that build (METHODOLOGY section 5); repeatable
  --allow-tier-c NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier C (other or unknown); only after
                        reg.loadContract, loadRoot and a harmless scratch
                        write succeeded; repeatable
  --progress-file PATH  append JSON progress lines of long reads
                        (n4_inventory) to PATH
  --allow-http-for-tests
                        permit http:// base URLs (fake station in tests only)

read_tools.name: n4_connect
read_tools.description: Open a session to one of the stations the operator configured at server start (replaces any previous session). The URL, credentials and TLS policy are fixed by the operator and cannot be chosen here. The station's real stationName must equal expected_station (default: the configured station NAME), or the session is closed. Reports the detected version (oBIX productVersion) and its tier: A (4.13/4.14) writes; B (4.15/4.3) and C (other or unknown) refuse writes unless the operator opted the station in.

expected_station.description: Required stationName; default: the station NAME

read_tools.name: n4_describe_session
read_tools.description: Report whether a station session is active, which station, its version tier, and the server mode. Works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_navigate
read_tools.description: List the children of a component (name, type, handle, has_children). depth > 1 nests grandchildren under a 'children' key. elapsed_ms is the load time. For a station inventory use n4_bql_query or n4_inventory instead: one navigate is one round trip per component. types (optional) keeps only children whose type is one of the given specs (e.g. bacnet:BacnetDevice) plus the path to them; each kept entry then carries matched true/false. has_children ignores the types filter: it is true when the entry has any component child, matching or not. types keeps a given type and its subtypes; types_note says when the registry could not be read. Each component or struct slot whose children are listed also lists the declared properties the station left out at their default (handle null), marked default: true with their value, or value null and a note when the type contract gives no default value; the sub-entries of a declared struct default are marked default too and may show type null. defaults_note says when a type contract could not be read, and names a declared default that could not be decoded (left out).

types.description: Optional type specs to keep, e.g. ['bacnet:BacnetDevice']; default: no filter

read_tools.name: n4_read_slots
read_tools.description: Read all slots of one component as {name, type, value, status}. Status complexes add status_ok/status_null; a Status slot's omitted value or status takes the type default. value_display carries the station's display string; a complex the reader cannot decode (e.g. a Modbus FlexAddress) returns that display string as value. elapsed_ms is the load time. A slot that is itself a baja:Status also adds status_flags, the names of the flags set; status_ok is false when any is set. A station leaves out a declared (frozen) property still at its default; those are listed after the loaded slots from the type contract (the station's type registry, read once per session), each marked default: true with the contract's default value, or value null and a note when the contract gives no default value (e.g. a component default such as proxyExt): never an invented value. defaults_note says when a type contract could not be read, and names a declared default that could not be decoded (left out).

read_tools.name: n4_list_links
read_tools.description: List baja:Link / baja:ConversionLink links of components up to depth levels below ord. source_path is null when the source handle is outside the loaded subtree.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_find_dangling_outputs
read_tools.description: List components (up to depth levels below ord) with an 'out' slot that no link in the subtree uses as a source. Links from outside the subtree are not seen. A source ORD that is neither a handle nor an absolute slot path cannot be resolved: outputs it may feed are listed as unknown, not dangling.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_bql_query
read_tools.description: Bulk read: one projected BQL select over a subtree, returned as rows (one HTTP GET, usually under a second, where a navigate crawl costs one round trip per component). Use it FIRST for any inventory. Only 'select <cols> from <type> [where ...]' is accepted; '|' is refused. Columns are the station's display headers (e.g. 'Slot Path', 'Name'; a localized station translates them, a repeated header becomes 'Type#2'); the queried name column is decoded ($20 -> space), 'Slot Path' stays ORD-ready. Proxy-extension fields project as proxyExt.<slot>, e.g. proxyExt.dataAddress. Rows are capped (truncated=true when cut).

base.description: Subtree ORD or slot path, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers (default: the station root)

query.description: select <columns> from <type> [where ...], e.g. select slotPath, name, out from control:ControlPoint

output_file.description: Optional plain file name (.csv or .json): the rows go to <state-dir>/bql/<name> (0600, never overwritten) instead of the reply

read_tools.name: n4_inventory
read_tools.description: Station inventory through three BQL queries: networks, devices and points below base (default /Drivers), counted per network and per device. A network's built-in local device slot (localDevice, e.g. SnmpNetwork's own agent) is flagged local=true and counted apart from field devices. progress lists each step's row count; the operator's --progress-file gets the same lines. A network is a driver:DeviceNetwork row at any depth, named by its path below base.

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per query in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_file
read_tools.description: Read one station file (e.g. a Px view file:^px/General.px) through the station's file servlet: GET /file/<path>. file_ord is a file:^ ORD or a path relative to the station home. Refused before any request: '..', '|', ':', absolute paths, directories, names ending in '.' or ' ' and .bog/.bog.gz (the station never serves them). Text types (px, xml, nav, chart, json, csv, html, txt, ...) return text; other files return size, sha256 and content type only (output_file saves the complete bytes under <state-dir>/files/). status is ok, forbidden (403: no read permission) or not_found (404); a 401 pauses station calls and is never retried. Reads are capped at max_bytes (truncated=true, sha256 null when cut).

output_file.description: Optional plain file name with an extension: the complete bytes go to <state-dir>/files/<name> (0600, never overwritten)

read_tools.name: n4_list_px_views
read_tools.description: List the Px views (baja:PxView) below root with one BQL query: display_name, px_file (the file:^ ORD to pass to n4_read_file / n4_px_summary) and media. A PxView is a property value, not a component, so the station usually answers its slot path as NULL: slot_path and owner_path are null then (see owner_note).

read_tools.name: n4_px_summary
read_tools.description: Fetch one .px file (like n4_read_file) and summarize it without returning the XML: media, imported modules, canvases and viewSize, layers, widget and binding type counts, bound ORDs grouped by component (a trailing value slot such as /out stripped), images, included Px files, charts, other ORDs and label texts. Every list is capped at max_items. A file larger than max_bytes is refused, not summarized in part.

read_tools.name: n4_list_batches
read_tools.description: List the write batches in this server's journal, newest first: batch_id, tool, station_name, ts, state (completed / in-doubt), verdict, rollback_of and rolled_back_by. Use it to find the batch_id for n4_rollback. A journal line that cannot be read is listed in unreadable and the reply says the list is incomplete. Reads the journal only; works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_session_retro_draft
read_tools.description: Draft the session retro: reads this server's audit and journal and returns markdown plus evidence-backed CANDIDATE kit deltas (refusals, bad read-back verdicts, in-doubt batches, BOX errors, dangling outputs). Proposes only; never applies or stages anything. An audit line that cannot be read is named in the summary, which says the draft is incomplete. The window starts at the server start; pass since (ISO-8601, e.g. 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for the whole history) to change it.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; only newer entries are considered (default: when this server started)

read_tools.name: n4_spy_page
read_tools.description: Read one diagnostics page of the station's spy tree (GET /ord?spy:/<path>, the pages the Workbench Spy view shows) as data: title, tables (title, header, rows of cells), links to child pages as relative spy paths, the POST actions the page offers (named only as spy paths without their query, never invoked) and the text outside tables. The content of a form field (textarea, select, button, input) is never returned, wherever it sits. Read-only: one GET under the spy root. Refused before any request: a scheme or ':' (except one module:Type segment directly under sysManagers/registryManager/types/, the registry's type pages, e.g. sysManagers/registryManager/types/control:NumericWritable), '|', '..', a query string ('?', '&', '=', '#'), '%', ';', a backslash, any Unicode control character, invalid UTF-8 and the known action pages (util/gc, util/forceThreadDump). status is ok, forbidden (the user may not read spy pages), not_found, not_html or parse_timeout (the page was not parsed within timeout_s). Spy pages are diagnostics: their layout differs between Niagara versions, so read the tables as found. The reply is bounded as a whole: truncated is true when a cap cut it and truncated_by names the caps (max_bytes, max_rows across all tables, tables, row_cells, links, actions, name, cell, text).

path.description: Path below the spy root, e.g. metrics, sysInfo or util/JMX Info; empty for the index

max_rows.description: Cap of table rows returned, all tables together

max_bytes.description: Byte cap of the page read

read_tools.name: n4_station_health
read_tools.description: Station health in one call, each section answered on its own: system (the SystemService slots by their station names: CPU usage in percent, memory as the station reports it plus memory_used_percent, version, host, time), points (total, ok, null_only, not_ok_count, a count per status flag in by_flag and the not-ok ones in not_ok, up to max_not_ok; ok is no flag, null_only is the flag null alone, a point with no value and not a fault, and not ok is any other flag, so ok + null_only + not_ok_count = total; proxy is the points whose proxy extension is not control:NullProxyExt, the ones a licence counts), networks and devices (the same, plus disabled and each not-ok entry's name, type and enabled), totals (the n4_inventory totals of the same rows, with rows_truncated when a query feeding them was cut), capacity (resources: the Global Capacity table of the spy metrics page, per resource used and limit, unlimited true where the station shows no limit, and live; recount: its recount times) and elapsed_ms. Two counts sit side by side in a resource: used is the licence's own tally, the number to quote against limit for licensing, and it only grows until a capacity recount or a station restart; live is what the station really holds now (networks, devices and proxy points of the whole station; null for a resource this tool does not count or when base is a subtree). may_be_inflated is true, with an inflation_note, when a used is above its live or the recount has never run. A section that fails is {error} and the others still answer. capacity is null with a capacity_note when the spy metrics page is unreachable or holds no Global Capacity table: never a guessed count. capacity_truncated is true, and capacity_note says so, when the page was cut before it was read whole, so resources may be missing; rows of the table that do not match its header are counted in capacity_note. In a section, truncated means not_ok was cut at max_not_ok (not_ok_count is whole) and rows_truncated means the query hit max_rows, so the counts are lower bounds. A status the station did not answer counts under the flag unknown and as not ok, never as ok. license is the licence manager page (spy sysManagers/licenseManager) in short: licenses (name, expires, valid, with state when not valid, and days_left counted from the station's own date, the day of system.systemTime; null for never, for an expiry that is not a date or when that date is unknown; up to 100, licenses_count when more), nearest_expiry (the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features, with same_date: how many share it), expired (what is already past; null when the station date is unknown) and a warning when the nearest expiry is 60 days away or fewer, or past, when a licence is not reported valid, or when an expiry could not be read as a date; note says what the reading could not do; {error} when the page was not read, saying which case it is (no permission, no such page, not HTML, not a licence page), never an empty licence. n4_license_info has the whole of it.

base.description: Subtree ORD of the point, network and device counts, default station:|slot:/

max_not_ok.description: Cap of the not-ok entries listed per section

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_history
read_tools.description: Read the last records of one history, newest first, to prove records arrive (a {ok} history extension proves it runs, not that records exist). Name the history by history_id (/<station>/<history name>, as historyConfig.id shows it) or by ext_ord (the history extension's ORD, e.g. station:|slot:/Folder/Point/NumericInterval, resolved to its id with one BQL select); give exactly one. Each row is {timestamp, value, status} as the station renders them (localized display text, e.g. '15 nov 2026 20:09:35 CST', '21,0', '{ok}'); columns are the station's headers. Optional range: period (today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate, lastYear) or start and/or end (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00), not both. truncated is true when the range holds more records than limit; total_records is the range's record count (select count(*)), null with total_records_note when that count failed. A history that cannot be read is an error naming the id and how to list the ids. Read-only: fixed queries over a history: ORD, no file output.

period.description: Period id: today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate or lastYear

end.description: Range end as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_license_info
read_tools.description: What the station's licence manager says, in one call (one GET of the spy page sysManagers/licenseManager, read-only): host_id; certificates (name, expires, valid); licenses (name, expires, valid, days_left) with license_kind, the qualifier the page gives them (e.g. perpetual); brand, owner and project (the tridium:brand and tridium:about features); maintenance (below); nearest_expiry, the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features (kind, name, expires, days_left, same_date: how many share that date); expired, what is already past (up to 50, expired_count when more); features (count, matched, list of name, expires and attributes by key, capped by max_features, truncated). valid is true only when the page writes the state valid; any other state is valid false with state, the text as written. expires is never, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or, when the page writes anything else, that text as written with days_left null: such entries are counted in note and are in neither nearest_expiry nor expired. Every days_left counts calendar days from the station's own date (station_date, the day of the SystemService systemTime, which must be a whole timestamp), never this machine's: 0 on the expiry day, negative once past, null for never or when the station date is unknown (station_date_note says why, and expired is null). maintenance is what the licence states of the software maintenance agreement (SMA): sma_attributes, one entry per feature that has sma.* attributes (feature, attributes by key), up to 50 with sma_feature_count; sma_exempt_features, the names of the features whose sma.exempt is true, each once, up to 50 with sma_exempt_count (an exemption of that one feature, never of the licence as a whole); sma_truncated when a list was cut; feature, a feature named after maintenance when there is one; and expires, the end date of the agreement: null unless a local licence file states it, because the page carries none. The page does not carry when a licence was generated nor its version: only when the server was started with --niagara-home NAME=PATH for this station (its Niagara installation directory, reachable from this machine) each licence adds generated and version, and maintenance adds expires, days_left and license from the maintenanceExpiration attribute, all read from the root element of the file of that licence's name under security/licenses and nothing else of it (never its features or signature). Only a regular file of exactly the licence's name is opened; generated_note says, per licence, why the facts are missing: no such file, a link or another non-regular file, a name that differs in letter case, a file over 1 MiB or not a licence, one issued for another host, or past the 100 files read in one call. A local file that matches no licence of the page is neither read nor named. status is ok, not_recognized (the page answered but is no licence manager page), or a spy status: forbidden (the user may not read spy pages), not_found, not_html, parse_timeout; only ok carries the licence fields, so an unreachable page is never an empty licence. A line of the page is read whole or not at all: note counts the lines that matched no known pattern (two entries on one line, a name with a bracket or brace, a heading out of place) and names a cut page, a missing section and a list that was cut. The reply is bounded whatever the page holds: every string taken from the page is stripped of control characters and cut with the marker ...[cut] (200 characters for a name, expiry, state or host id, 64 for an attribute key, 100 for its value), a feature keeps 30 attributes (attributes_truncated), 100 certificates and 100 licences are read (certificates_count, licenses_count when the page has more), every list also stops at a byte budget, and the whole reply stays under 2 MiB for any page up to the 2 MiB read cap.

feature.description: List only this feature: an exact vendor:name (e.g. tridium:bacnet), else every feature whose name holds the text; compared without case

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_station_runtime
read_tools.description: What the station is running, in one read (read-only): uptime, from the spy page sysInfo: boot_time, current_time and up_time as the station writes them (localized text) and uptime_s, the seconds between its bootTicks and currentTicks; loaded_modules, from the spy page sysManagers/moduleManager, which lists only the module parts the station has loaded: count and modules (name, vendor, version), up to max_rows, truncated when cut; jars_on_disk: the session lists no module jars, so its status is unavailable (note says why) unless the server was started with --niagara-home NAME=PATH for this station (its Niagara installation directory, reachable from this machine): then the .jar files of PATH/modules (modules_dir, count; a link or other non-regular file is never opened and is named in skipped), with the root attributes of META-INF/module.xml read only from the jars that may hold a loaded part and from those changed after the boot (versions_read; jars whose module.xml cannot be read are named in unreadable; complete is false then or when the scan stopped at 5000 jars or timeout_s). mismatches (up to max_rows, mismatch_count, mismatches_truncated; null without the jars): module, reason, loaded_version, disk_version, jar and jar_modified, where reason is version_differs (the jar holds another version than the loaded one), modified_after_boot (same version, but the jar changed after the boot), loaded_not_on_disk (no jar holds the loaded part) or not_loaded_modified_after_boot (a jar of no loaded part changed after the boot). The boot is this machine's clock minus uptime_s, compared with the jar times of this machine's filesystem, with 2 s of slack. restart_needed is true with any mismatch, false only when the uptime, the whole loaded list and every jar are known and none differs, and null otherwise; restart_note says which. A spy page the user may not read is that section's status (forbidden, not_found, not_html, parse_timeout, with a hint), never a failed call; a page without the measured layout is not_recognized with a hint.

max_rows.description: Cap of the loaded modules and of the mismatches listed, each

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds; also bounds the reading of the jars

read_tools.name: n4_read_alarms
read_tools.description: Read the station's alarm records, newest first: by default the open ones (unacknowledged or not back to normal). Each row is {timestamp, uuid, source, source_state, ack_state, alarm_class, priority, msg_text} as the station renders them (display text, e.g. '7 nov 2026 09:20:50 CST', 'Offnormal', 'Unacked'; msg_text may be a raw %lexicon(...)% pattern); columns are the station's headers. Filters, all optional and combined with and: source (a component ORD such as station:|slot:/Drivers/Net; matches it and everything below it), alarm_class (a class name such as defaultAlarmClass), source_state (normal, offnormal, fault, alert), ack_state (acked, unacked, ackPending), since and until (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00). A source_state or ack_state filter replaces the open default; open_only false reads every record. where echoes the BQL where clause sent; truncated is true when more records match than limit; total is the matching record count (select count(*)), null with total_note when that count failed. Every filter value is checked before any request: no quotes, wildcards or BQL of the caller reach the station. Read-only: fixed queries over the alarm: ORD.

source.description: Component ORD whose alarms to read, itself and below, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers/Net

source_state.description: One of normal, offnormal, fault, alert

since.description: Oldest alarm time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00 or 2026-11-15T06:00:00Z

until.description: Newest alarm time as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00

open_only.description: true (default) reads only open alarms (unacked or not normal) unless a state filter is given; false reads every record

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_list_alarm_classes
read_tools.description: List the station's alarm classes with their priority per transition ({toOffnormal, toFault, toNormal, toAlert}, 0-255), whether each transition needs an acknowledgement (ack_required), their alarm counts, and the recipients each one routes to. Recipients are the alarm:AlarmRecipient components (console, email, station and others) and a class routes to one through a link from the class's alarm topic to the recipient's routeAlarm action; each class lists {path, type, link_name} of its recipients, recipients lists each recipient with the classes linked to it, and unresolved_links the routeAlarm links whose source is not a listed class. At most 50 recipients are read for links (recipients_truncated says when more exist). A value the station renders in another form is returned as its text. Read-only: two BQL selects at the station root and one tree load per class folder and recipient. To create a class, see the README recipe (n4_create_component, n4_set_slot, n4_create_link).

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_commissioning_report
read_tools.description: What is still wrong or unfinished below scope, in one call (read-only; about 11 station reads for the whole station whatever its size: one BQL query per table, one link scan, three slot loads and the licence page). The reply starts with summary, one line per section (ok / N finding(s) / not checked: why / skipped: why, with the truncation note), then requests (the station reads made) and each section: state (ok, findings, partial: clean in the checks that ran while others did not run, not_checked, skipped), findings (absent when no check ran) and checks. A check that ran is {count, items, more}: items are the first limit offenders as {path, name, fact} and more is how many the limit left out; a check that did not run is {not_checked: why} (a failed or impossible read: never a zero) or {skipped: why} (not asked for). Every fact is a value the station answered. points: the control points per status flag (in_fault, down, stale, disabled, overridden, in_alarm, null_output, status_unreadable); devices_down_or_disabled lists the devices that are down, disabled or in fault first, their points counted in their flags and not listed (under_listed_devices); networks_not_ok; by_network counts devices and points per driver network. histories: points_without_history (the points with no history extension below them: with expect_histories they are listed and are findings; without it the check is a count with the note pass expect_histories to list them, no list and not a finding), and the history extensions that are disabled, in_fault or never_recorded (lastRecord.timestamp null). alarms: points_without_alarm (only with expect_alarms), unknown_alarm_class (an alarm extension whose alarmClass names no class below Services/AlarmService), classes_without_recipient (no link from the class's alarm topic seen within three levels of the AlarmService), open_alarms and unacked_alarms (the classes with any, alarms is their sum). links (one scan link_depth levels below scope): unresolved_source (a source ORD that is neither a handle nor an absolute slot path, or a slot path that does not exist; source_outside_scan counts the sources not judged), inputs_with_several_links (a priority input in1..in16 targeted by more than one link), dangling_outputs (the check of n4_find_dangling_outputs; unknown counts the outputs it cannot decide). naming: duplicate_display_names among sibling points, escaped_names ($xx in the slot name), palette_default_names (a point of the control palette such as NumericWritable or BooleanPoint1, or a point called by the name of its own type plus the number the station appends, such as a kitControl:Tstat called Tstat1; a lone Tstat is not flagged). station (only when scope is the whole station): services_in_fault, licence_expiry (the warning of n4_station_health's license section), and unsaved_changes and last_backup, always not_checked with the reason: the station does not expose them to a read. Bounds: each query reads at most max_components rows; a truncated table sets truncated and truncated_note (truncated at N components: counts are lower bounds and absences are not asserted; narrow the scope), and a check that would assert an absence from it is not_checked; a link scan over max_components is not judged.

scope.description: Slot path to report on, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers/BacnetNetwork; default the whole station

sections.description: Sections to build; default all of them

limit.description: Offenders listed per check (the count is always whole)

expect_histories.description: Which points should have a history extension: {kinds: [numeric, boolean, enum, string, writable], name_pattern: a glob such as *Temp* over the name or display name}, {} is every point; without it points_without_history is a count only

expect_alarms.description: Which points should have an alarm extension, same shape as expect_histories ({} is every point); without it points_without_alarm is skipped

link_depth.description: Component levels below scope the link scan reads (1-4); the scan loads link_depth + 3 levels of slots, so keep it low on a large scope

max_components.description: Hard cap of the rows read per query and of the components a link scan may hold

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_list_schedule_kinds
read_tools.description: Which kinds of schedule a station can hold and how each works, so no type name has to be known (reads no station, needs no session). schedule_kinds: boolean, numeric, enum, string (weekly schedules with special events: out follows the weekly time ranges, special events override them, a default output fills the rest), calendar (a list of days other schedules reference) and trigger (fires a topic at times of day on chosen days); each with its station type, value_type, the plain value it takes, default_output, which parts it has (weekly, special_events, dates, times), purpose, behaviour and what its out is usually linked to (by convention a writable's in16). event_kinds: date, date_range, week_and_day, custom and reference (the days of a calendar), each with its type, purpose, whether a calendar can hold it (in_calendar) and its fields with their allowed values. Also priority (top special event first), cleanup (passed date and date-range events are deleted by the station) and export_import (the station types that copy schedules between stations; no tool here).

read_tools.name: n4_read_schedule
read_tools.description: One schedule decoded into plain JSON (one load; read-only), for every kind n4_list_schedule_kinds lists. kind and type; for boolean, numeric, enum and string schedules: out, next_time, next_value, default_output, in and facets (each value is {value, status}: value true/false, a number, an enum ordinal or a string, null when the status is null; status ok, null or the station's encoding), out_source (what drives out: Input, Special Event: <name>, Week: <day> or Default Output), effective (always, or the date range rule of the effective period), weekly (monday to sunday, each a list of {start, end, value} sorted by start, times HH:MM with end 24:00 for a range that runs to midnight; a range the station holds without a value is listed with value null and ignored true, since the station skips it) and special_events in priority order (name, kind, rule, priority 1 = highest, ranges). Rules by kind: date {year, month, day, weekday}, each "*" when it matches any; date_range {start, end} (two date rules); week_and_day {month, week, weekday}; custom {year, months, days, weeks, weekdays} (lists, empty = any); reference {calendar: the calendar ORD}. Months are jan..dec, odd, even; weekdays sunday..saturday; weeks week1..week5, last7days, calendarWeek1..calendarWeek6, before_last7/14/21. calendar: out, next_time, next_value and dates (name, kind, rule). trigger: enabled, times (HH:MM), dates, last_trigger and next_trigger. Every slot the station leaves out because it holds its default is filled from the station's type registry; a slot neither sent nor described is an error, never a guess. last_modified is the station's time of the last change.

ord.description: The schedule component's ORD, e.g. station:|slot:/Schedules/Lobby

read_tools.name: n4_read_tags
read_tools.description: Read the tags of one or more components (ord, or ords: up to 50). Per component: direct tags (metadata slots, as {id, namespace, name, type, value, slot, flags}; the slot name is the escaped id, hs:point is hs$3apoint), tag_groups (each an n:tagGroup relation to a group definition, {group_ord, slot}), direct relations ({id, endpoint_ord, inbound, slot}) and, unless implied is false, the implied tags the station's dictionaries compute ({id, type, value}; a tag group's tags appear here). relations: direct (default), all (adds the implied relations, such as n:parent and n:child) or none. One load per component, plus one session call each for implied tags and implied relations.

ords.description: Several component ORDs (1 to 50), read in order

implied.description: Also read the implied tags (default true)

relations.description: direct (default): the relation slots on the component; all: also the implied relations; none: no relations

read_tools.name: n4_neql_query
read_tools.description: Find components by their tags with a NEQL query (one GET of base_ord|neql:<query>|view:file:ITableToCsv, the documented ORD route). neql is a filter such as n:point, hs:equip and not hs:ahu, tst:label = "hello", hs:temp > 20, n:name like ".*Pump.*" or a relation path (n:parent->hs:floor = 2); implied tags count. It matches the components below base_ord (default station:|slot:/), never base_ord itself, and returns their station ORDs (ords). With bql (one select, e.g. select slotPath, out.value) the station runs that select on the matches and the reply carries its columns and rows instead. '|' is refused (the ORD separator); a query the station cannot parse is HTTP 400, reported as such. max_rows (default 200, at most 2000) bounds the reply; truncated says it was cut.

neql.description: NEQL filter, e.g. hs:point and hs:temp

base_ord.description: Search below this component ORD (default station:|slot:/)

bql.description: Optional select run on the matches, e.g. select slotPath, out.value

read_tools.name: n4_list_tag_dictionaries
read_tools.description: List the tag dictionaries installed under the TagDictionaryService (one BQL query), each with its namespace, enabled, frozen, version and status, and what it defines: tag definitions (id, info type, value type, default, validity condition; type null for a smart tag the station computes), tag groups (id, the group_ord a tag group relation points at, the tags it implies) and relation ids. dictionary (a name such as Niagara, or a namespace such as n) lists one. max_items (default 200, at most 2000) bounds the definitions listed across all dictionaries; truncated says some were left out. Use it before n4_set_tags to see which tags, values and groups a station defines.

write_tools.name: n4_create_component
write_tools.description: Add a component under parent_ord (optionally with a wire sheet position). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

name.description: Requested slot name (the station may rename on collision)

wire_sheet.description: Optional {x, y, w} wire sheet annotation (integers; w defaults to 8)

proxy_ext.description: Optional driver proxy extension type spec (e.g. modbusCore:ModbusClientNumericProxyExt) to create a point with; configure its address afterwards with n4_set_slot

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_add_history
write_tools.description: Add one history extension per point, already configured: historyName (baja:Format pattern), enabled and, for mode interval (the default), interval (ms), in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 50 points). Mode cov adds a change-of-value extension instead, which records each change of the point value and has no interval. The extension type follows the point type read from the station (numeric, boolean, enum or string control point: NumericInterval / NumericCov, BooleanInterval / BooleanCov, EnumInterval / EnumCov, StringInterval / StringCov), and so does its default slot name. Refuses a point that is not one of those, an ext_type that does not fit the point, a point that already has a child named ext_name and, when the pattern only uses %name%/%parent...name% tokens, a history id (/<station>/<history name>) that would repeat in the batch or that an extension on the station already holds (one BQL read). The capacity argument sets the history capacity in records (Roll when full) or unlimited, by a set op on historyConfig/capacity right after each add in the same batch; without it the extension default stays (500 records). The plan notes how long the capacity lasts at the interval. The read-back checks the type, the configured slots, the capacity when given, the history id and that the extension is not in fault. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

points.description: Point ORDs (1 to 50), each gets one extension

history_name.description: baja:Format pattern for the history name, unique per device, e.g. S%parent.parent.parent.name%_%parent.name%

interval_ms.description: Sampling interval in milliseconds (300000 is 5 minutes); required for mode interval, refused for mode cov

mode.description: interval: sample every interval_ms; cov: record each change of value (no interval). Default: the mode of ext_type when given, else interval

capacity.description: History capacity: a number of records (the oldest roll off when full; 20160 is 7 days at 30 s) or "unlimited". Default: the extension default, 500 records

ext_name.description: Slot name of the extension under each point; default: the extension type's short name, e.g. BooleanInterval

ext_type.description: History extension type; default: the one that fits each point's type, and a type that does not fit is refused

enabled.description: Start collecting at once (true) or leave disabled

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_add_alarm
write_tools.description: Add one alarm extension per point, already configured, in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 50 points). Every palette alarm extension is an alarm:AlarmSourceExt whose offnormalAlgorithm and faultAlgorithm follow its kind: out_of_range (numeric point: high/low limits, deadband, limit texts, and fault limits on its faultAlgorithm; giving a limit enables it), numeric_change_of_state (numeric: alarm_values), boolean_change_of_state (boolean: alarm_value), boolean_command_failure (boolean), enum_change_of_state and enum_command_failure (enum: alarm_values for change of state), string_change_of_value (string) and status (any control point). Without kind, the point type read from the station picks it: numeric out_of_range, boolean boolean_change_of_state, enum enum_change_of_state, string string_change_of_value. Each extension is added with its plain slots (alarmClass, sourceName, toOffnormalText, toFaultText, toNormalText, timeDelay, timeDelayToNormal, hyperlinkOrd), then set ops in the same batch swap both algorithms by type and set alarmEnable, alarmInhibit and the algorithm slots by path. Texts are baja:Format patterns resolved against the alarm record: %alarmData.sourceName%, %alarmData.presentValue%, %alarmData.highLimit%, %alarmData.lowLimit%, %lexicon(module:key)%, %% for a literal percent; %parent...% does not resolve in the state texts (it does in source_name). Refuses a kind that does not fit a point (naming the kinds that do), an algorithm argument the kind does not take, an alarm_class the station does not hold (one BQL read; the refusal lists the existing classes), a child already named ext_name and a second extension of the same kind on a point unless allow_second. The read-back reads every slot it set and both algorithm types, and lists under coerced each slot the station stored differently ({slot: {sent, read}}, verdict mismatch). Alarm recipients, routing and acknowledging are other tools' work. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

points.description: Point ORDs (1 to 50), each gets one alarm extension

kind.description: Alarm extension kind; default: the one that fits each point's type (numeric out_of_range, boolean boolean_change_of_state, enum enum_change_of_state, string string_change_of_value); a kind that does not fit is refused

ext_name.description: Slot name of the extension under each point; default: the palette name of the kind, e.g. OutOfRangeAlarmExt

high_limit.description: out_of_range: offnormalAlgorithm/highLimit; giving it sets limitEnable/highLimitEnable true

low_limit.description: out_of_range: offnormalAlgorithm/lowLimit; giving it sets limitEnable/lowLimitEnable true

high_limit_text.description: out_of_range: baja:Format text of a high-limit alarm; it overrides to_offnormal_text, e.g. %alarmData.sourceName% high: %alarmData.presentValue% > %alarmData.highLimit%

low_limit_text.description: out_of_range: baja:Format text of a low-limit alarm; it overrides to_offnormal_text

fault_high_limit.description: out_of_range: faultAlgorithm/highLimit, above which the point goes to fault (toFaultText); giving it sets faultAlgorithm/limitEnable/highLimitEnable true

fault_low_limit.description: out_of_range: faultAlgorithm/lowLimit, below which the point goes to fault; giving it sets faultAlgorithm/limitEnable/lowLimitEnable true

alarm_value.description: boolean_change_of_state: the value that is in alarm (default true)

alarm_values.description: numeric_change_of_state, enum_change_of_state: the values in alarm as tag -> ordinal, e.g. {"alarm": 1}; sent as the baja:EnumRange {alarm=1}

to_offnormal_text.description: baja:Format text of the alarm when the point goes offnormal

to_fault_text.description: baja:Format text of the alarm when the point goes to fault

to_normal_text.description: baja:Format text when the point returns to normal

source_name.description: baja:Format source name of the alarms; default on the station: %parent.displayName%

alarm_class.description: Slot name of an alarm class under the AlarmService (it must exist)

alarm_enable.description: Transitions that generate an alarm (alarmEnable, sent as the hex bit mask offnormal 1, fault 2, normal 4, alert 8); default on the station: all

time_delay_ms.description: timeDelay: how long the point must stay offnormal before the alarm, in milliseconds

time_delay_to_normal_ms.description: timeDelayToNormal: how long the point must stay normal before the return to normal, in milliseconds

inhibit.description: alarmInhibit: true inhibits the alarms (sent as a baja:StatusBoolean, status ok)

hyperlink_ord.description: hyperlinkOrd: an ORD the alarm console links to

allow_second.description: Add the extension even when the point already has one of the same kind

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_copy_component
write_tools.description: Copy one configured component (e.g. a Modbus device with its points and their addresses) under the same parent once per new name, in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 30 copies). The copy holds the type, plain slots and child components up to 6 levels deep. Runtime slots are left out by flags read from the station's type definitions: a frozen slot declared readonly, transient or default-on-clone (e.g. status, health, out, read and write values) or made transient, and a dynamic slot flagged transient or remove-on-clone; flags an integrator set otherwise travel with the copy. The plan notes list each slot left out with its flags, calling out a readonly slot that holds a non-default value; actions, slots the station lists by name only and links are not copied either; a deeper source is refused. The read-back compares each copy's whole configured subtree with the plan. The source may carry station escapes (Numeric$20Writable40001); new names are plain. Change what differs per copy afterwards (e.g. deviceAddress with n4_set_slot). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

parent_ord.description: ORD of the parent that holds the source and receives the copies

name.description: Slot name of the source child under parent_ord

new_names.description: Distinct plain slot names, one per copy (the station may rename on collision)

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_set_slot
write_tools.description: Set one slot to a value. Status slots are always written whole (value and status). A slot the station omits because it holds its type default is typed from the station's type definition (registry channel), so a default-valued property such as a history extension's enabled, historyName or interval can be set. A nested slot is a path from ord (grp/sp). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

slot.description: Slot name, or a path of slot names separated by / for a nested slot; must be listed by the station or declared by its type

value.description: New value by value_type: a number (Double, StatusNumeric), true/false (Boolean, StatusBoolean), a string (String; Format takes its pattern, e.g. %parent.name%), or a whole number of milliseconds for RelTime (300000 is 5 minutes), a whole number for Integer (Java int range), or for Simple the encoded string of the type (a whole number is sent as its decimal string, e.g. a Modbus address 40014 on dataAddress/address) (an enum tag such as signedInteger or modbus, a Facets string such as units=u:celsius;...|precision=i:1, a LinearConversion scale;offset such as 0.1;0.0). A struct such as a Modbus FlexAddress is set through its child slots (dataAddress/addressFormat, dataAddress/address)

value_type.description: One of baja:Double, baja:Boolean, baja:String, baja:StatusNumeric, baja:StatusBoolean, baja:Format, baja:RelTime, baja:Integer, baja:Simple

simple_type.description: Only with baja:Simple: the type spec module:Type to send the value as when it replaces the slot's current type (e.g. driver:LinearConversion for a proxy conversion); default: the slot's own type

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_set_flags
write_tools.description: Set the flags of one slot of a component: either flags, the complete new set that replaces the current one (an empty string clears every flag), or add and/or remove, letters changed in the current set so the letters the slot already holds are kept. The plan shows the current and the requested flags with their names; the inverse restores the previous flags exactly, and the read-back loads the slot again and compares the two sets. Refused: both forms or neither, an unknown or repeated flag letter, a letter both added and removed, a slot the component does not have, a set equal to the current one, and a slot whose current flags cannot be read (not sent by the station and its type contract unreadable). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

slot.description: Name of one slot of that component (a property, an action or a topic); not a path

flags.description: The complete new flag set as letters, each once, in any order; "" for no flags. Letters: r readonly, t transient, h hidden, s summary, a async, n no-run, d default-on-clone, c confirm-required, o operator, x execute-on-change, f fan-in, A no-audit, p composite, R remove-on-clone, m metadata, N non-critical, L link-target, 1 2 3 4 user-defined

add.description: Instead of flags: letters to add to the slot's current flags, each once (same letters as flags)

remove.description: Instead of flags: letters to remove from the slot's current flags, each once (same letters as flags)

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_invoke_action
write_tools.description: Invoke a control action. Only set, active, inactive, auto, and ping (a driver network, device or point device ext checks its device; no setting changes) are allowed in this version. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

arg_type.description: baja:Double or baja:Boolean, only for set

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_create_link
write_tools.description: Create a link from a source slot to a target slot. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_remove_component
write_tools.description: Remove the child `name` of parent_ord with its whole subtree. The plan snapshots the subtree to depth 3 (type, plain slots, wsAnnotation, links inside it) as the inverse; n4_rollback can re-create only that snapshot, not a full restore. The dry run scans the write-scope prefix that holds parent_ord (or link_scan_ord) to depth 6 for links from the subtree into components outside it; when it finds any it refuses unless acknowledge_links is true, and then records them so n4_rollback re-creates them. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

link_scan_ord.description: Optional ORD equal to or under the write-scope prefix that holds parent_ord; it narrows the link scan, never widens or moves it. By default the scan covers that prefix; when the prefix holds more than 100000 nodes to depth 6 the dry run refuses and asks for this narrower root

acknowledge_links.description: true removes even though the scan found links from the subtree into components outside it (the dry run lists them); false (default) refuses such a remove

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_rollback
write_tools.description: Undo a journaled batch by running its recorded inverse through the same dry run / token pipeline, as a new batch linked to the original. Refuses unknown, already rolled back, in-doubt and other-station batches. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

batch_id.description: batch_id returned by an earlier write

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_save_station
write_tools.description: Save the station (persist the running config to disk). The BOX reply proves nothing; persisted is true/false/unknown from config.bog when the server has --station-home for this station. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_ack_alarm
write_tools.description: Acknowledge alarm records by uuid (1 to 100, as n4_read_alarms returns them), with optional notes, through the station's alarm channel (ackAlarms): the station sets the acking user, the ack time and ackState ackPending, updates the alarm database and routes the ack. The dry run reads each record first and refuses, naming them, any uuid with no record, any record whose source is outside the write scope (or is not a slot path), and any record already acknowledged or ack pending. The read-back re-reads the records: verified when none is still unacked and each has a user; mismatch when any stayed unacked or the station names alarm classes the user may not acknowledge (it needs operatorWrite on the record's class; those names are returned in observed.permission_failed_classes). An acknowledgement cannot be undone: there is no inverse and n4_rollback cannot reverse it. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

uuids.description: Alarm record uuids (1 to 100), e.g. b65e6bcf-0b8a-4d0c-9a77-3c1d2e4f5a6b

notes.description: Notes added to each alarm with the acknowledgement

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_set_tags
write_tools.description: Add, change or remove direct tags on 1 to 50 components (ords) in one batch. add: [{id, value?, type?}] where id is ns:name; a tag the installed dictionaries define takes the definition's value type (a type that differs is refused) and, without value, its default; a Marker takes no value. A tag no dictionary defines is refused unless allow_ad_hoc is true, and never allowed in an installed dictionary's namespace (the Tagging guide: an ad hoc tag must not use an existing dictionary's namespace). A new tag is added as a metadata slot (flag m, named ns$3aname); a tag already there with another value of the same type is set (a type change is refused: remove, then add); one already holding the value is skipped with a note. remove: [id] removes direct tags (the inverse re-adds each with its type, value and flags). add_groups / remove_groups: [id] apply or remove a tag group an installed dictionary defines (a relation n:tagGroup to the group's definition, flag r, as Workbench adds it); the station then implies the group's tags, and the read-back lists the target's implied tags and any group tag missing from them. add_relations / remove_relations: [{id, endpoint_ord}] add or remove an outbound relation to another component (written as its handle ORD h:...), the id defined by a dictionary or, with allow_ad_hoc, in a namespace of its own. A group or relation already on the target, one missing from a remove, an entry named twice, or one both added and removed is refused. At most 200 ops (targets x changes), each target under the write scope. The read-back reloads each target and reports values the station normalized under coerced (sent 4.50, stored 4.5). It removes tags and relations, so it is in the destructive class (destructiveHint). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run; n4_rollback undoes the batch.

add.description: Tags to add or change: [{id: "ns:name", value?, type?}]

allow_ad_hoc.description: true allows a tag or relation no installed dictionary defines, in a namespace no dictionary installs

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)
